title: The empty frame, found
logline: The 8×10 black frame from March 2001, in a thrift-store bin with something in it at last. What's in it is reserved. The page draws the bin, the frame, and the light on the glass, which hides it.

panels.composition: A thrift store's bin of frames, tilted, a hand-lettered $2 tag. Among them, the plain black 8×10 from 2001, and there is something in it now — a photograph, a paper, a drawing — but the window's light lies across the glass in a white sheet and hides it completely. The page refuses to tilt it.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a thrift-store bin of secondhand picture frames with a hand-lettered two-dollar tag, one plain black eight-by-ten frame among them with something inside that a sheet of white window glare across the glass completely hides, no people, no words
image.notes: Reserved: what is in the frame. The glare is the device.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: 'I'll know when I see it.' He did, apparently. We don't.
